reviews.title: So disappointing
reviews.text: Our family tried three different apps to work on Spanish and to compare experiences across platforms. Speak is very much the worst of the three. So many programming and interface build errors. Constant buffering and slow advance between screens regardless of connection strength. Frequently mis-hears accurate speaking and responses. Bizarre jumps into entirely new content before teaching vocabulary, context, or syntax. Frequent confusion with random introduction of multiple tenses too quickly, before solidifying present tense understanding. Very disappointed in Speak and recommend opting for other apps over this one.

reviews.title: Slow, boring. Not for fast learners.
reviews.text: Wow. This was… a journey. Between the AI voice rounding robotic and pronouncing words in Spanish incorrectly (it’s incapable of a silent H in “hasta luego”) and the incredibly SLOW user interface, I can’t handle this. There’s no way as far as I can tell to test into higher levels without a premium subscription, so I’m starting at the beginning. I say this with love and kindness: if you consider yourself to be an average learner or someone who struggles, this is for you. If you were a pleasure to have in class that made the honor roll: this is absolutely not for you. Repetition of single phrases over and over within the same lesson isn’t actually helpful when it causes you to be so bored that you check out completely. I’m shocked this app has so many good reviews. I’m trying to be fluent, not a tourist.

reviews.title: Recurring Lesson Loading Issue
reviews.text:
I paid for a one-year subscription, but lately the app has become extremely frustrating to use. Very often, when I tap on a lesson, it just keeps loading indefinitely and never opens.

It doesn’t happen every single time, but it has been happening so frequently recently that I often can’t study at all. For a paid annual subscription, this is really disappointing.

The app may have good content, but that doesn’t matter much if the lessons are not reliably accessible. I hope the developers fix this issue soon.

AI 맞춤형 어쩌구해서 발음 교정이나 어법 교정에 도움될까 해서 제대로 배워보려고 1년 구독밖에 없지만 진행했는데, 한달 사용해보니 실질적으로 제가 원한 방법이 전혀 아니라 구독을 취소 했습니다. 환불은 안하려고 그 달에 몇번 쓰고 그냥 말았는데, 세번째 결제내역 보고 결제가 계속된 걸 알았어요.
결제 내역이 스픽이나 애플 해외결제도 아니고 NICE_통신판매 로 결제돼서 뭔지 몰랐는데 화가 나서 환불요청하고 결제 정보 삭제하려는데 결제 변경에는 결제수단 추가? 이딴 것만 있고 결제정보 삭제나 구독 결제 취소 같은 건 없어요. 심지어 제대로된 고객센터도 없고 음침한 방법을 사용하는 기업입니다. 

이용해준 고객을 기만하는 두 번 다시 소비하지 않을 회사입니다.

reviews.title: 只能全自動一直往前跑要怎麼學習？
reviews.text:
當初訂閱的時候很正常啊，一句唸完要點一下才會進到下一個，後來有了免手持自動開關也可以，反正可以用自己要的方式學習
現在是怎麼了，開發團隊被裁光了全用AI決策是不是，很多課程變成只能全自動不斷的往前跑，我唸錯了，還在想，不順等等之類的都無視，馬上就進到下一個句子，連重新嘗試練習的機會都沒有
我請問一下這樣怎麼學習？學習不就是要讓人反覆嘗試練習嗎？想一下又怎麼了，多想幾次熟能生巧啊。是不是你們的團隊都只用自己母語在測試所以覺得這樣好棒棒，還是根本都是AI在設計，AI反正根本不知道人類為什麼要練習

還有那個新字彙的設計也是爛到炸，常常一口氣整個課程全是專有名詞是怎樣，怎麼學習。而且過度強調在地用語，這邊的使用者是要學外語還是學外國母語啊，你會丟一堆網路用語來做為老外中文教材嗎？五樓你說看看

反應了非常多次都沒用，已退訂

reviews.title: Too many inaccuracies, AI slop
reviews.text: I used this app to learn Spanish and I’m sure it helped me to speak more confidently. However, I’m using it now to brush up on French which I’ve studied extensively in the past and after just a few lessons I’ve realized that it tries to teach phrases/grammar that nobody would actually use, and rejects things used in everyday speech. I also noticed a few things which were blatantly wrong in the Spanish lessons, and I shudder to think of how many incorrect things I and other people learned in that course that went by unnoticed. Overall I now think this app is AI slop that’s not worth the subscription cost.

reviews.title: Things you should know .
reviews.text: Speak only provides about maybe five or six languages for you to learn. Some of them include English Spanish Korean Italian and maybe one more language, but I was more looking forward to practicing German and I was kind of disappointed that they do not have German at all, so if you would like to learn more than those languages, I just said then I would not recommend he speak. Right now I’m learning Spanish, which is kind of right I guess. But I just feel like speak is. It’s making you learn too fast. You know it’s kind of hard to memorize and that. Yeah I’d give me 2 to 3 stars. I’ve definitely tried a different or better apps like Duolingo. I think Duolingo is better so.

reviews.title: Is this a joke?
reviews.text: I’m having a hard time telling if this is a joke. For a free app that has in app purchases for the premium upgrades, it doesn’t give you more than 3 questions about the weather for the “trial”. You can’t move beyond 3 questions without signing up for the pricey subscription. Other learning apps have a basic learning section that’s free AND a more detailed learning experience with their subscriptions. Reading the reviews I thought this would be even better than those options, especially since money is tight these days. But to think not a single review has mentioned this little “teaser trial” as I call it because you aren’t going to really know if you like the app if you can’t even get past the same 3 questions without money. Either that’s a new very debilitating feature, or I question the validity of the other reviews.  I highly recommend everyone try this app just for the sheer experience of seeing for yourself that it’s not what everyone in these reviews is saying. Don’t take my word for it, truly see the scam for yourself.

reviews.title: Comparing two different apps
reviews.text: I can’t agree that Duolingo is not the ideal language learning app. But when I saw an ad comparing the two I had assumed that I was able to learn a language without having to pay a monthly fee or anything like that just like Duolingo. But to find that I can only do two lessons and then I have to go premium was very disappointing. In my opinion, it should not be compared to do Duolingo and ads due to the misconception that Duolingo is technically free while this app is not. Otherwise, the lessons were great, just very disappointed in the fake advertisement of the comparison with Duolingo 😔💀

reviews.title: Dont speak
reviews.text:
I wanted to like Speak. I really did. The idea—practice a language by actually speaking it—sounds great on paper. In reality, the app feels like a glossy demo that never quite becomes a real product.

The conversations are repetitive and shallow, like talking to a chatbot that learned language from a handful of scripts. You say a sentence, it nods approvingly, and you move on—whether or not you actually understand what you just said. There’s very little correction, nuance, or explanation, which makes it hard to improve beyond parroting phrases.

The onboarding promises fluency-through-speaking, but most of the experience feels locked behind a paywall, and even then the value doesn’t scale. After a few sessions, you realize you’re cycling through the same patterns with different words swapped in. It’s more like a pronunciation toy than a serious learning tool.

Worst of all, it gives you the feeling of progress without the substance. You walk away thinking you practiced, but when it’s time to actually use the language in real life, you’re stuck.

reviews.title: Lost my trust so quick
reviews.text:
The ads I’m seeing for this app, promising you’ll understand “the whole Bad Bunny album in ten days” and be “fully native in 2.5 months,” are so packed with lies it basically forces you to stop taking anything they say seriously.

Language does not work like that. Anyone who has actually learned one knows it. Music is full of slang, cultural references, wordplay, rhythm, and emotional context. You don’t “unlock” that in ten days unless your definition of understanding is reading a loose translation and nodding along.

What bothers me most isn’t just that these claims are false. It’s that they feel deliberately dishonest. They prey on people’s frustration, impatience, and insecurity, then promise magical outcomes they know are impossible. At that point, it stops being marketing and starts being manipulation.

It also makes me question everything else about the app. If they’re comfortable saying things this untrue in ads, what else are they stretching or fabricating? Are the testimonials real? Are the reviews cherry-picked or manufactured? Or is this just another case of “say anything, get the subscription, deal with disappointment later”?

This kind of advertising doesn’t just hurt users. It hurts trust in language learning as a whole. It makes people feel stupid when the promised results don’t happen, and it pushes them to quit altogether, convinced the problem is them, not the lie they were sold.

Learning a language takes time, exposure, confusion, repetition, and patience.
